newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures down on Wall St, await Tankan.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures down on Wall St, await Tankan.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended a little lower on Tuesday after an overnight fall on Wall Street.
Dealers said the market's next direction would be set by the Bank of Japan's "Tankan" report on corporate sentiment which is due to be published on Wednesday morning.

The report, which is widely expected to show that the business outlook is bearish, particularly in the manufacturing sector, was cited by several dealers as a reason for staying away from the futures market.
"Everyone's eyes are on the Tankan now," said one dealer.
The Nikkei 225 September contract settled at 20,375 points, down 35 on the day and at the top of a broad band of support between 20,300 and 20,400 points.

Technical analysts said they were comforted by the fact that the Nikkei had not been shaken by the large fall in New York overnight, where the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 192 points to 7,604 in its second largest single-day drop ever.
The fall followed comments by Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto about potential sales of U.S. Treasures by Japan.
The June MSCI Taiwan index contract also shrugged off the fall in New York, rising 0.5 points to 382.5 on 1442 lots by 0700 GMT.
